title: Affine completed kernel annihilation makes the completed coherent ideal product zero
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $I,K$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaves, and $a:F\to G$ a morphism of coherent modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let $t\in\mathbb N$. For every affine open $U$, take the inverse limit $a_U$ of the section maps of the $I$-adic quotient system of $a$ (positive level $n+1$). Suppose $K(U)^t$ annihilates $\ker(a_U)$. Then $H=K^t\ker(a)$, with the image definition of ideal product [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], is coherent and $H/I^{n+1}H=0$ for every $n\geq0$. No completion equivalence or local faithfulness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 088A (lemma-existence-tricky), second application of Remark 0888; affine finite-module calculation via Tag 087W and Algebra Tag 00MB. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088A, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0888 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00MB.

proof.text: The coherent kernel L of a has quasi-coherent ideal-power product H. Its inclusion into L is mono, so Noetherian coherence stability for quasi-coherent submodules proves H coherent. The t=0 power is the unit sheaf.

On each affine U, formalCompletion_affine_sections supplies the quotient isomorphisms and the completion isomorphism. Compose the latter with preservesLimitIso for evaluation to identify the section-system limit with AdicCompletion. Naturality is proved by checking all limit projections, choosing a lift of each quotient class and cancelling the canonical quotient projections. Mathlib AdicCompletion.map_injective then makes the completed section map of any mono into a coherent module injective. F has finite affine sections by the finite-type criterion and restriction of finite local generators.

Construct the canonical map from sections into their quotient-system limit by the quotient projections. Its naturality and kernel.condition show that each section of L maps into the kernel of the limit map for a. The affine product range identifies H(U) with K(U)^t times L(U). The hypothesis kills the limit image of every generating scalar multiple; additive induction kills all product sections. Apply injectivity of the completed inclusion H to F from the preceding step to conclude that each section of H has zero canonical completion image. This needs only injectivity of completion on inclusions, not a completed-kernel equality or tensor-product flatness.

Project the zero canonical completion image to level n to make every affine section quotient projection zero. The affine quotient comparison makes this projection surjective, hence every affine quotient section module is zero. For each open W cover W by affine opens contained in W and apply sheaf separatedness to any section and zero. Thus the identity of each positive quotient is zero, proving IsZero. This also covers empty schemes, the unit completion ideal and t=0; no faithfulness is used.

lean.statement: theorem coherentKernel_idealProduct_completion_zero {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData) (F G : CoherentModules X) (a : F ⟶ G) (t : ℕ) (h : ∀ U : X.affineOpens, K.ideal U ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) (LinearMap.ker (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight ((completion X I).map a).hom (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op U.1)))).hom)) : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 (kernel a.hom)) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (formalModuleQuotient I (n + 1) (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 (kernel a.hom)))
